title: Adapters & ergonomics: v1→v2 migration docs, streaming examples, and changelog automation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a compact, example-first migration and docs package for SDK v1→v2 focusing on: (1) adapter patterns that let existing code keep working while opt-ing into v2 ergonomics, (2) clear streaming ergonomics examples across Python/TypeScript/Go, (3) concrete retry semantics changes and recommended configs, and (4) an automated changelog extraction spec and scripts to surface deprecations and behavioral changes for downstream consumers. The output should be consumable by developer PMs, SDK maintainers, and Solutions Engineers.
background: During the v2 redesign we introduced ergonomic API changes for streaming, a stricter retry policy, and renamed several client configuration fields. Customers and examples across repos still reference v1 patterns; we need a migration surface that reduces breakage and documents tradeoffs so teams can upgrade on their cadence. Past migration tickets focused on broad migration guides; this ticket is specifically about adapter libraries, small copy-pasteable examples for three languages, and an automated changelog pipeline that aggregates labeled PRs and deprecation markers into a single migration digest.
acceptance_criteria: A set of lightweight 'adapter' shims for Python/TS/Go that allow v1-style callsites to compile/run with v2 client while emitting a single deprecation warning.
Documentation pages: migration overview, streaming ergonomics migration, retry semantic changes, and a examples gallery with runnable snippets for each language.
Changelog automation: a scripted job that tags PRs with 'sdk-v2-change' and emits a one-page migration digest (markdown) in the releases repo when a release branch is cut.
QA: integration test that runs adapter examples against the hosted API sandbox and verifies parity on a representative prompt and streaming events shape.
Engineering signoff and a short post-mortem checklist for future deprecations.
implementation_notes: Design adapter modules as thin wrappers that translate v1 method names to v2 equivalents and normalize streaming event shapes; avoid copying core client logic into adapters.
For Python: provide both sync/async adapters; prefer context-manager usage for resources; explicit buffer flush configuration for streaming.
For TypeScript: provide a small helper that polyfills back-compat streaming callbacks into async iterators and vice-versa.
For Go: provide an interface-compatible adapter type that implements the v1 interface but delegates to v2 internals; include example using go modules and replace directives.
Retry behavior: document new default of 3 attempts with exponential backoff; surface a helper that maps old retry knobs to new RetryPolicy objects.

Changelog automation: use PR label 'sdk-v2-change' and scope labels (python|ts|go|streaming|retry) to generate categorized migration notes. Job runs on release branch creation and on merges to main (draft).
migration_examples:
PYTHON EXAMPLE (adapter) # v1-style callsite stays the same; adapter translates to v2 client from redwood_sdk_v2.adapters import LegacyClientAdapter client = LegacyClientAdapter(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}") # old callsite: response = client.completions.create(prompt="Hi") # adapter maps to v2 streaming API under the hood and returns a simple object response = client.completions.create(prompt="Hello") print(response.text) TYPESCRIPT EXAMPLE (streaming iterator)
// v1 used onMessage callbacks; v2 yields async iterator events import { makeLegacyStream } from '@redwood/sdk/v2/adapters' const stream = makeLegacyStream({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY }) stream.on('data', (chunk) => console.log('chunk', chunk)) await stream.start('Hello') GO EXAMPLE (interface shim) // Provide a type that satisfies old Client interface but forwards to v2 client package adapters // example usage in cmd/app.go: client := adapters.NewLegacyClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY")) Note: these examples will be published with runnable links and tests in the examples repo.
changelog_automation_spec:
Behavioral spec:
1) Maintain a lightweight GitHub Action that runs on PR merge. Contributors must add label 'sdk-v2-change' to PRs that modify SDK surface or behavior. Additional scope labels: 'python', 'typescript', 'go', 'streaming', 'retry', 'deprecation'.
2) Action extracts PR title, body, labels, and optional '/migration-note' footer in the PR description. It posts a summarized entry to the 'sdk-migrations' artifact (markdown) and adds the PR to an in-progress migration digest.
3) When a release branch is created (tagged sdk-v2.x), a second job compiles all collected entries into a single migration_draft.md, organized by scope and severity (breaking|behavioral|deprecation).
4) The run uploads the draft to the releases repo and opens a PR targeting the docs site for review.
Implementation: use a small Node script that consumes the PR payload and updates a JSONL state file in .github/migrations/ (state file used only by CI).
rollout_plan: Week 1: Implement adapter prototypes and publish them to internal registry for consumption by Canary teams.
Week 2: Draft docs pages and examples; run first integration test against sandbox; collect feedback from Solutions Engineering.
Week 3: Implement GitHub Action for changelog automation and validate on a test repo; iterate on PR labeling guidance.
Week 4: Merge docs, publish adapter packages, and announce migration digest with upgrade checklist.
test_plan: Unit tests for each adapter that assert compatibility with v1 callsites and correct invocation of v2 client methods.
Integration test: start a local sandbox that simulates streaming events and validate example output shapes across languages.
CI check: run changelog extraction script against a curated set of historical PRs to ensure no false negatives/positives.
Manual QA: Solutions Eng will run the examples in a workshop with two customers and report any blocking gaps.
